abstract: We aimed to determine how marker density influences the detection and localization of quantitative trait loci (QTLs) in rice and to identify parental alleles with consistent effects across genetic backgrounds and environments. We evaluated grain yield, plant height, and flowering time in four interconnected recombinant inbred line populations at two Brazilian sites, Goianira and Boa Vista. Each parent contributed to two crosses, allowing us to compare the direction of its allelic effects in different genetic backgrounds. We compared a common backbone of 2,060 DArTseq SNPs with denser, cross-specific panels using marker and bin regression, interval mapping based on genotype probabilities inferred by hidden Markov models, and genome-wide permutation thresholds. The backbone recovered the major QTL regions. Peak positions differed by less than 100 kb in 14 of 19 comparisons within crosses and environments, including five exact matches. Across the four maps, densification increased marker counts 4.66-fold and recombination bin counts 2.44-fold. Recombination-breakpoint interval width decreased by 31.1% in Maninjau/Epagri 108 and 90.3% in Irat 122/Araguaia. Comparisons using the same lines resolved an apparent peak shift at qPH12 and placed qYLD2 below the genome-wide threshold in both panels. Four QTL regions recurred across crosses. Epagri 108 contributed all of them for reduced height at qPH1, whose interval contains SD1, and delayed flowering at qDTH8. Araguaia contributed an allele for earlier flowering at qDTH3 in both its crosses. The qDTH6 region recurred in Goianira, and the opposite flowering effects observed across environments in Irat 122/Araguaia mapped to different chromosome 6 peaks. Grain-yield QTLs showed less recurrence. The strongest associations, qYLD1 and qYLD6, occurred in separate indica/japonica crosses. In Goianira, qYLD6 explained 32.5% of phenotypic variance in the full-panel analysis and achieved genome-wide significance only at that site. Parental genome sequences helped prioritize candidate genes. Two complementary recombinants delimited a 247.0-kb region containing Ef-cd at qDTH3, while Hd1 and OsCLF remained genetically unresolved within a 51.8-kb marker-defined interval at qDTH6. These findings identify Epagri 108/Araguaia as a candidate cross for combining reduced height with earlier flowering. For grain yield, the favorable Maninjau allele at qYLD1 and Epagri 108 allele at qYLD6 warrant testing individually and together in recipient backgrounds under target growing conditions. Because the backbone was derived retrospectively, its economic benefit requires prospective evaluation. For routine marker-assisted selection, breeders could genotype founders and initial mapping families at high density, use a common panel of markers representing recombination bins to track validated haplotypes across subsequent families, and add cross-specific flanking markers to select progeny that retain a favorable allele within a smaller donor segment.
authors: Prado, J. F. F. d. S.
